title: Presentability of a Cartesian fibration with presentable fibers
statement: Use the universes and monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and presentability of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a Cartesian fibration in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], classified by $G:\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ with fibers $\mathcal E_b$. Assume $\mathcal B$ and every $\mathcal E_b$ are presentable, every Cartesian restriction $G(f):\mathcal E_{b'}\to\mathcal E_b$ is a right adjoint, and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$, $G$ carries every small $\kappa$-filtered colimit diagram $b:I\to\mathcal B$ to a limiting cone $G(\operatorname{colim}_I b)\simeq\lim_{I^{\mathrm{op}}}G(b_i)$. Then $\mathcal E$ is presentable and $p$ is accessible, meaning that $p$ preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$. The base and total categories may be large in the smaller universe; their presentability is relative to that smaller universe, with all objects contained in a sufficiently large universe.
